html:
Three closures cost a first-timer a whole day, and no ticket page warns you. The Vatican Museums close on Sundays, except the last Sunday of the month, when entry is free from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. (last entry 12:30 p.m.) and the crowd is the month’s largest; they also close on about a dozen church holidays, among them 29 June, 14–15 August, 1 November and 8, 25 and 26 December. ◇ So the Vatican day is never a Sunday. Ostia Antica, the fourth-day ruin (Decision 09), and the Borghese Gallery both close on Mondays, ◇ which makes Monday the natural day for the ancient core. And winter shortens the afternoon: from late October to the end of February the Colosseum closes at 4:30 p.m., with last entry at 3:30, ◇ so the ancient half-day is a morning. The dates for your trip are on the Field Sheet.

Strikes are the other rhythm, and they are announced, not sprung: Italian transport strikes are listed in advance on the transport ministry’s strike calendar. ◇ On a strike day Rome’s buses, trams and metro run only in guaranteed bands, until 8:30 a.m. and from 5 to 8 p.m.; ◇ trains run to a list of guaranteed services that Trenitalia posts for each strike, so check it for the airport train. What a strike means for you is simple: it costs rides, not sights. Walk the core, which you were doing anyway; take the fixed-fare taxi to or from the airport; and move a Vatican or Ostia ride into the guaranteed hours, or to another day.
